_comment: Overworld biomes. move_hours = hours to cross one region tile (about 3 miles) on foot, off-road. glyphs are picked per tile for texture. 'local' controls what the local map looks like when you enter.

ocean.name: open sea
descriptions: Grey water to the horizon, heaving and cold.
The sea, restless and the colour of slate.
Open sea, and the wind coming off it smelling of salt and distance.
Water, and more water, and a line of weather on the edge of it.
The sea: grey-green, cold, and not interested in you.
Whitecaps as far as you can see, and a gull hanging over them.

lake.name: lake
descriptions: A wide stretch of still, dark water.
Lake water, brown with peat and very cold.
A long lake, reed-fringed, with mist lying on it in the mornings.
Still water that holds the sky, and something moving under it now and then.
A mere, black and deep, with a drowned tree at the edge.
Open water with a wind across it and small waves slapping the stones.

coast.name: coast
descriptions: Shingle beaches and dunes, stinking of rotting kelp.
A windy shore of sand, gravel and gull-cries.
Salt marsh and mudflat, where the tide goes out a mile and comes back fast.
Low cliffs and a strip of stony beach, the grass on top bent flat by the wind.
A coast of coves and wrack, and fishing-boats hauled up above the tideline.
Dunes held together with marram grass, and the sea loud behind them.

plains.name: grassland
descriptions: Open grassland under a wide sky, grazed short by sheep.
Rolling pasture and old field-strips, hedged with thorn.
Flat country of hay-meadow and ditch, a church tower in every direction.
Common grazing and scattered farms, the tracks rutted deep.
Big fields and small copses, and the sky doing most of the work.
Open plain, the grass long and grey-green, rippling when the wind goes over.

forest.name: forest
descriptions: Old oak and ash wood, dim and quiet, thick with bramble.
Broadleaf forest where the paths are narrow and the light is green.
Deep woodland, the old trees wide as houses and the ground thick with leaf.
A wood of hazel coppice and old oak, full of paths that go nowhere.
Beech wood, grey-trunked and quiet, the floor bare under the canopy.
Wildwood, tangled and wet, where nobody has cut anything in a lifetime.

pine_forest.name: pine forest
descriptions: Dark ranks of pine, resin-scented, the ground soft with needles.
Conifer forest, silent but for the wind in the crowns.
Fir forest, close and dark, snow lying under it long after it has gone elsewhere.
Tall pines on rocky ground, and the smell of resin in the cold.
Spruce so thick that noon looks like evening under it.
A pinewood of fallen trunks and moss, and the sound of water somewhere below.

hills.name: hills
descriptions: Bare, sheep-bitten hills of heather and scree.
Rolling uplands cut by stony becks and drystone walls.
High moor of peat and bog-cotton, the paths marked by cairns.
Green hills folded one behind the other, each with its sheep and its stone wall.
Rough upland of gorse and bracken, with old workings on the slopes.
Downs of short turf and chalk, and barrows along the ridges.

mountains.name: mountains
descriptions: Steep, broken mountainside, loose stone underfoot and wind that never stops.
Crags and gullies where a slip means a long fall.
Mountain country: scree, snowmelt torrents and paths a goat would think twice about.
Grey peaks close above you, cloud tearing on them.
High valleys of rock and thin grass, and the roar of water everywhere.
Cliffs and ledges and a wind that tries to take you off them.

high_mountains.name: high peaks
descriptions: Snowfields and bare rock above the clouds, thin-aired and deadly cold.
The high peaks: ice, wind and silence.
Ice and rock and nothing else, the air too thin to hurry in.
A world of white, and the sun off it like knives.
Glaciers grinding down between black ridges.
Wind-carved snow and bare stone, where nothing lives that can leave.

marsh.name: marsh
descriptions: Sucking fen and reedbed, loud with insects, the water brown and foul.
Marshland where the path is wherever the ground holds you.
Wet country of alder carr and black pools, the paths on old causeways.
Reed and sedge to the horizon, and the cry of birds you cannot see.
Bog, where the ground quakes and the water smells of eggs.
Drowned land, half water and half mud, with willows standing in it.

tundra.name: tundra
descriptions: Treeless barrens, frozen hard, the wind carrying ice.
Flat, pale waste of moss and frost under a low sky.
Frozen plain, the ground cracked into shapes by the cold.
Lichen and bare stone and wind, under a sky that never seems to end.
Tundra: low scrub, standing water frozen at the edges, and nothing tall for miles.
A hard, open land where the only shelter is what you carry.

desert.name: scrub desert
descriptions: Dry scrub and dust, the ground cracked and glaring.
Sand and thornbush, and no water anywhere you can see.
Broken badlands, red and dry, the gullies full of thorn.
Stony waste where the heat comes up off the ground like breath.
Dust and dry grass and the bones of something by the track.
A dry country of dunes and dead river-beds.

glacier.name: glacier
descriptions: A glacier: a river of old blue ice, groaning as it moves, the snow on it hiding cracks you will not see.
Ice to the horizon, ridged and fissured, and a wind off it that takes the breath out of you.
The great ice: white, blinding, silent but for a crack now and then like a door slammed in a cold hall.
Snow lying on ice lying on rock, and nothing alive, and the sun no warmer than the moon.
A frozen plain where the ice is a mile thick, and the old people say the dead of the first winter sleep in it.
Seracs and crevasses, blue in their depths; every step tested, every step a guess.

steppe.name: steppe
descriptions: The steppe: grass to the edge of the world, silver where the wind combs it, and a sky too big to look at.
Feather grass and wormwood, the smell of it bitter and clean, and the horizon flat as a blade.
Open grassland without a tree or a wall, where a rider is a speck for an hour before he reaches you.
Dry, rolling grass, the burial mounds of forgotten khans standing up out of it like islands.
A sea of grass under a hard blue sky, larks overhead and the wind never once stopping.
Short, tough grass and a few stone figures on the old mounds, all of them looking east.

savanna.name: savanna
descriptions: Golden grass to the shoulder, and flat-topped thorn trees standing far apart in the heat-shimmer.
The savanna: dry grass, red earth, termite towers taller than a man, and herds moving on the skyline.
Grassland burnt yellow by the sun, a lone thorn tree, and the shadow of a vulture going over it.
Heat, dust, and the hum of insects in the long grass, and something watching from the shade.
A wide hot country of grass and thorn, where the waterholes are known and fought over.
Red dust and yellow grass and the white bones of something big, picked clean by the noon.

jungle.name: jungle
descriptions: Jungle: green on green on green, dripping, and the noise of a thousand things you cannot see.
Trees like towers, roped together with lianas, and the light down here the colour of deep water.
Hot, wet, rotten-sweet air, and every path closing behind you as soon as you have cut it.
A green dusk at noon, monkeys shrieking in the canopy and the ground alive with ants.
Steaming forest of giant leaves and hanging roots, where the rain falls every afternoon like a curtain.
The jungle: beautiful and patient, and it would very much like to eat you.

dunes.name: sand sea
descriptions: The sand sea: dunes the height of hills, rippled by the wind and moving as slowly and surely as glaciers.
Sand, sand and sand, gold in the morning and white at noon, and the heat coming up off it like an oven.
Great dunes marching to the horizon, their crests smoking in the wind.
A desert of nothing but sand and sky, where the only shade is your own shadow.
Dunes that sing when the wind is right, a low hum like a giant's sleep.
Endless sand and a white sun, and the mirage of water always just a mile ahead.

badlands.name: badlands
descriptions: Badlands: red rock carved into towers and tables and gullies, and not a drop of water in any of them.
Mesas and buttes standing out of a red plain, striped like a cut cake.
A maze of dry gullies and crumbling red cliffs, the ground glittering with bits of crystal.
Broken red country, hot and silent, where the wind has carved the rock into things that look like faces.
Hoodoos and arches and dry washes, and the bones of beasts no one has seen alive.
Rust-coloured hills, bare as a skinned hide, and a hawk circling over them.

salt_flat.name: salt flat
descriptions: A salt flat: white and dead level to the horizon, cracked into plates, the glare of it painful.
The bed of a sea that dried before men came, white crust crunching underfoot.
Salt, white as bone, flat as a table, and the mountains floating on a mirage at the edge of it.
A blinding white pan where nothing grows and the wind tastes of tears.
Salt crust over black mud; break through and the mud holds on.
A flat white waste, so still that the sky lies on it like water.

volcanic.name: volcanic waste
descriptions: Black rock and grey ash, steaming vents, and the smell of rotten eggs and hot iron.
A land the fire made: old lava frozen in ropes and waves, and the ground warm under your boots.
Cinder cones and fields of black glass, and a red glow somewhere ahead in the smoke.
Ash to the ankle, and the sky dark with what the mountain breathes out.
Steam hissing out of cracks in black stone, yellow sulphur crusted round them.
A burnt land, still smoking, where nothing has grown since the mountain last woke.

fey_forest.name: enchanted wood
descriptions: An enchanted wood: the trees are silver and the leaves glow, and the paths are never where you left them.
A forest where it is always dusk, lights drifting between the trunks, music just too far off to follow.
Pale trees, moss like velvet, and the feeling of being watched by something amused.
The wood the old stories warn of: lovely, and wrong, and the birds here sing words.
Glowing mushrooms in rings, and a silence that listens back.
A wood out of a dream: every tree a little too beautiful, every glade a little too still.
